content.text:
This is already a fairly polished, accessible single-page template (SEO meta tags, dark/light theme toggle, scroll-spy nav, skip link). A few concrete gaps I could fix:

1. **theme-color meta tags** don't update when the user manually toggles the theme (they only follow `prefers-color-scheme`) — the browser chrome color can mismatch the page.
2. **Placeholder content** (title "My Page", `hello@example.com`, `example.com` URLs, generic section text) — needs real copy for it to be usable.
3. No `<html lang>` alternative or `noscript` fallback message.
4. `og:image` points to a nonexistent asset.

Which direction do you want — polish the technical details (#1, #3, #4) and leave content as-is, or should I fill in real content for a specific site/project?
